## New Columns on Existing Tables

```sql
-- Q6: ratification gate flag per-agent
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN flags text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT ARRAY[]::text[];

-- Q28: cohort-baseline scoring during runs 1-5
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN forge_template_id uuid;
CREATE INDEX idx_agents_forge_template ON agents(forge_template_id);

-- Q41: per-agent budget override
ALTER TABLE cost_tracking ADD COLUMN budget_override numeric(10,2);
ALTER TABLE cost_tracking ADD COLUMN budget_override_approved_by text;
ALTER TABLE cost_tracking ADD COLUMN budget_override_approved_at timestamptz;

-- Q33: full provenance per training_patch
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN signal_id uuid;
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN pattern_ids uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT ARRAY[]::uuid[];
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN prompt_diff_sha text;
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN predicted_delta numeric(5,3);
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN actual_delta numeric(5,3);

-- Q22: cross-patch attribution flags
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN attribution_unclear boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN attribution_conflict boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;

-- Q19: regression history per author/source
ALTER TABLE training_patches ADD COLUMN author_regression_history boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
```

## Realtime Channel Set (Q21)

5 named channels. All HR agents subscribe; per-agent filtering done client-side.

| Channel | Source events | Subscribers |
|---|---|---|
| `hr.runs` | `agent_runs` INSERT | Witness, Roster, Tutor |
| `hr.flags` | Witness antipattern + `incidents` INSERT | Cadence, Tutor, Mira |
| `hr.lifecycle` | `agents.status` UPDATE + lifecycle `agent_events` (promote/PIP/retire) | All HR + Yash digest |
| `hr.patches` | `training_patches` + `training_cycles` INSERT/UPDATE | Mira, Cadence, Witness |
| `hr.escalations` | rows matching Q10 paging criteria | Yash device + Cadence backup |

Enable with:
```sql
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agent_runs;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE incidents;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agents;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agent_events;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE training_patches;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE training_cycles;
```

Polling fallback per Q25: each HR agent maintains a 30s heartbeat. >2min missed → fall back to 60s polling on the source table; on channel restoration, re-sync via `created_at > last_seen_at`.

## Migration order

1. Create new tables (no FK conflicts with existing tables).
2. ALTER existing tables to add columns.
3. Add RLS policies (default: service_role full access; all other roles deny by default).
4. Enable Realtime publications.
5. Backfill `agents.forge_template_id` from existing Forge metadata if available; NULL is acceptable for legacy agents.
6. Verify with `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md` §"Verification protocol".

# HR Constitution v1 — Schema Additions (2026-04-27)

The 50 ratified Q-decisions in `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md` require the following additions. All follow standard project conventions: RLS on, indexes on FKs + frequently queried columns, `updated_at` trigger, soft-delete via `deleted_at` only when needed.

## New Tables

### `hr_arbitration` (Q1 — Witness↔Cadence tribunal)
```sql
CREATE TABLE hr_arbitration (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  agent_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  opened_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  closing_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT (NOW() + INTERVAL '48 hours'),
  witness_payload jsonb NOT NULL,
  cadence_payload jsonb NOT NULL,
  tribunal_score numeric(4,3),
  resolution text CHECK (resolution IN ('witness_wins','cadence_wins','escalated_to_yash','timed_out')),
  resolved_at timestamptz,
  resolved_by text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_hr_arbitration_agent ON hr_arbitration(agent_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_hr_arbitration_open ON hr_arbitration(closing_at) WHERE resolved_at IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE hr_arbitration ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

### `training_locks` (Q2 — Tutor↔Witness interlock)
```sql
CREATE TABLE training_locks (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  agent_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  cycle_id uuid REFERENCES training_cycles(id),
  locked_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  locked_until timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT (NOW() + INTERVAL '24 hours'),
  released_at timestamptz,
  reason text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_training_locks_active ON training_locks(agent_id) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_training_locks_until ON training_locks(locked_until) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE training_locks ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

### `pending_flags` (Q2 — Witness flags queued during training_lock)
```sql
CREATE TABLE pending_flags (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  agent_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  flag_type text NOT NULL,
  payload jsonb NOT NULL,
  apply_after timestamptz NOT NULL,
  resolved_at timestamptz,
  resolution text CHECK (resolution IN ('fired','dropped_resolved_by_patch','dropped_pattern_change','expired')),
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_pending_flags_apply ON pending_flags(apply_after) WHERE resolved_at IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE pending_flags ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

### `dispatch_vetoes` (Q3 — Roster veto log)
```sql
CREATE TABLE dispatch_vetoes (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  agent_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES agents(id),
  task_id text NOT NULL,
  task_priority text NOT NULL CHECK (task_priority IN ('P0','P1','P2','P3','P4','P5')),
  severity text NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('WARNING','BLOCK')),
  reason text NOT NULL,
  proceeded boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  outcome text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_dispatch_vetoes_agent_created ON dispatch_vetoes(agent_id, created_at DESC);
ALTER TABLE dispatch_vetoes ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

### `forge_proposals` (Q4 — pre-deploy similarity hold)
```sql
CREATE TABLE forge_proposals (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  proposed_name text NOT NULL,
  proposed_spec jsonb NOT NULL,
  similarity_scores jsonb NOT NULL, -- {axis_skills, axis_tools, axis_model_tier, axis_mandate, composite}
  highest_overlap_agent_id uuid REFERENCES agents(id),
  status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pending_cadence_signoff','approved','rejected','auto_deployed')),
  cadence_decision text,
  cadence_decided_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_forge_proposals_status ON forge_proposals(status);
ALTER TABLE forge_proposals ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

### `pattern_conflicts` (Q5 — Mira contested patterns)
```sql
CREATE TABLE pattern_conflicts (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  pattern_a_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES proposed_patterns(id),
  pattern_b_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES proposed_patterns(id),
  domain_tag text,
  opened_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  sla_due timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT (NOW() + INTERVAL '7 days'),
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'contested' CHECK (status IN ('contested','resolved','consolidated')),

## Realtime Channel Set (Q21)

5 named channels. All HR agents subscribe; per-agent filtering done client-side.

| Channel | Source events | Subscribers |
|---|---|---|
| `hr.runs` | `agent_runs` INSERT | Witness, Roster, Tutor |
| `hr.flags` | Witness antipattern + `incidents` INSERT | Cadence, Tutor, Mira |
| `hr.lifecycle` | `agents.status` UPDATE + lifecycle `agent_events` (promote/PIP/retire) | All HR + Yash digest |
| `hr.patches` | `training_patches` + `training_cycles` INSERT/UPDATE | Mira, Cadence, Witness |
| `hr.escalations` | rows matching Q10 paging criteria | Yash device + Cadence backup |

Enable with:
```sql
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agent_runs;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE incidents;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agents;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agent_events;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE training_patches;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE training_cycles;
```

Polling fallback per Q25: each HR agent maintains a 30s heartbeat. >2min missed → fall back to 60s polling on the source table; on channel restoration, re-sync via `created_at > last_seen_at`.

## Migration order

1. Create new tables (no FK conflicts with existing tables).
2. ALTER existing tables to add columns.
3. Add RLS policies (default: service_role full access; all other roles deny by default).
4. Enable Realtime publications.
5. Backfill `agents.forge_template_id` from existing Forge metadata if available; NULL is acceptable for legacy agents.
6. Verify with `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md` §"Verification protocol".

## Realtime Channel Set (Q21)

5 named channels. All HR agents subscribe; per-agent filtering done client-side.

| Channel | Source events | Subscribers |
|---|---|---|
| `hr.runs` | `agent_runs` INSERT | Witness, Roster, Tutor |
| `hr.flags` | Witness antipattern + `incidents` INSERT | Cadence, Tutor, Mira |
| `hr.lifecycle` | `agents.status` UPDATE + lifecycle `agent_events` (promote/PIP/retire) | All HR + Yash digest |
| `hr.patches` | `training_patches` + `training_cycles` INSERT/UPDATE | Mira, Cadence, Witness |
| `hr.escalations` | rows matching Q10 paging criteria | Yash device + Cadence backup |

Enable with:
```sql
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agent_runs;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE incidents;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agents;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE agent_events;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE training_patches;
ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE training_cycles;
```

Polling fallback per Q25: each HR agent maintains a 30s heartbeat. >2min missed → fall back to 60s polling on the source table; on channel restoration, re-sync via `created_at > last_seen_at`.

## Migration order

1. Create new tables (no FK conflicts with existing tables).
2. ALTER existing tables to add columns.
3. Add RLS policies (default: service_role full access; all other roles deny by default).
4. Enable Realtime publications.
5. Backfill `agents.forge_template_id` from existing Forge metadata if available; NULL is acceptable for legacy agents.
6. Verify with `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md` §"Verification protocol".

108	  GROUP BY pu.agent_id, pu.skill_key
109	  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
110	)

112	  skills = (

78	## Composite Scoring System
79	
80	Every agent run gets a weighted composite score (0-100), computed inline by Witness at log time (no database triggers).
81	
82	| Component | Weight | Metric | Score Logic |
83	|-----------|--------|--------|-------------|
84	| Gate pass rate | 40% | gates_passed / (gates_passed + gates_failed) | 0-100 scale |
85	| First-try success | 30% | Did it pass all gates on first attempt? | 100 if yes, 0 if no |
86	| Rework cycles | 20% | Number of retries before success | max(0, 100 - (retries × 20)) |
87	| Yash override rate | 10% | Was output overridden by Yash in last 14 days? | 100 if no, 0 if yes |
88	
89	Witness **computes composite_score inline** before writing to `agent_runs`:
90	
91	```
92	gate_pass_rate = gatesPassed.length / (gatesPassed.length + gatesFailed.length)
93	first_try = firstTrySuccess ? 1.0 : 0.0
94	rework_factor = max(0, 1.0 - (reworkCycles * 0.2))
95	override_factor = 1.0 - (overrides_in_14_days / total_runs_in_14_days)
96	
97	composite = round(
98	  (gate_pass_rate * 40) +
99	  (first_try * 30) +
100	  (rework_factor * 20) +
101	  (override_factor * 10)
102	)
103	```
104	
105	### Scoring Rationale
106	
107	Why these weights?
108	- **Gate pass rate (40%):** The most objective measure — did the code compile, pass lint, pass tests? This is the foundation of quality.
109	- **First-try success (30%):** Efficiency matters. An agent that gets it right on the first attempt saves time and cost. Heavily rewarded.
110	- **Rework cycles (20%):** Retries consume tokens and time. Penalizes agents that need multiple attempts, but less than gate failures.
111	- **Yash override rate (10%):** The human check. If Yash had to correct the work, the agent missed something. Low weight because overrides are rare and subjective.
112	
113	These weights can be tuned by Yash. Update here AND in `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/config.json` (scoring.weights section) if changed.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

# Pod D — Shopify Website Department (8 agents) — Build + Train Plan

## Context

Boldteq currently has **Pod B (Shopify Native embedded admin apps)** and **Pod C (Shopify External standalone apps via Hydrogen RR7)**. Neither covers the third real workload: **client-owned Liquid themes** — Boldteq engineers who get CLI access to a client's Shopify store via GitHub, take an approved Figma design from elio/pixel, and convert it into a fully-dynamic Liquid theme pushed to the client's staging/live theme.

This is a net-new department, not a refactor. It closes 4 mapped coverage gaps:

1. **No Figma-to-Liquid converter** exists. elio outputs JSON specs for Pod B / Pod C consumers; nobody currently converts approved Figma to Liquid theme code.
2. **No Shopify theme CLI ops owner.** Bolt covers Railway / Docker / Shopify app-extension deploy, but not `shopify theme push/pull/dev` workflows or per-client GitHub-to-theme sync.
3. **No metafield / metaobject schema architect.** Dato is Postgres-only; no agent today owns Shopify content modeling for client storefronts.
4. **No storefront-side QA + reviewer.** Luna / Sage have admin-app review + test playbooks (Stack B audit checklist 509 lines, Stack B test suite 439 lines) but no storefront-theme equivalent (Lighthouse on storefront, theme-check, customizer settings smoke, cross-browser PDP).

The 8 new agents inherit **HR Constitution v1** (50 ratified Q-decisions in `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md`) Tier 1 from day 1, so all governance (arbitration, freshness SLAs, RACI, cost breakers, north-star) applies automatically. No HR-side work needed beyond Forge's Q4 similarity check (which passes — zero collisions on all 8 names).

Outcome: client theme builds run end-to-end inside the factory (intake → Figma loop → conversion → CLI push → UAT → publish → post-mortem) without any handoff back to humans except the client UAT itself.

## How To Use

1. Yash ratifies plan via ExitPlanMode (or overrides any agent name / mandate / cohort split).
2. Forge runs Q4 4-axis similarity gate on all 8 specs (composite < 0.60 confirmed by exploration).
3. Forge auto-deploys all 8 to Probation (cohort) per HR Constitution Q26 (parallel `probation_tracker` instances).
4. Mira drafts the Q30 4-artifact onboarding package per agent (prompt + charter + runbook + registry entry + pattern links).
5. Tutor pre-loads each agent with the skill-bank curriculum below as P3 batch (Cadence-approved training requests).
6. Witness watches first 10 runs each via cohort-class signal de-dup (Q26).
7. Cadence weekly review applies Q27 5-axis graduation gate.
8. Quarterly calibration (Q49) re-evaluates pod composition.

---

## Department Registration

**Department name:** Shopify Website Department
**Sub-department under:** Engineering (sibling to Pod A / Pod B / Pod C)
**Pod label:** `pod-d`
**Stack assignment:** `shopify-liquid-theme`
**Reports to:** Arya (Engineering VP)
**HR governance:** Cadence (cross-pod via HR Constitution v1)

**Distinguished from siblings:**
| Pod | Stack | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Pod A | Next.js + Supabase + Railway | Boldteq SaaS web apps |
| Pod B | React Router 7 + Polaris (CDN) + Prisma | Embedded Shopify admin apps |
| Pod C | React Router 7 + Tailwind + Hydrogen | Headless / standalone Shopify storefronts |
| **Pod D** | **Liquid + Online Store 2.0 + theme JS + Tailwind/CSS + Shopify CLI** | **Client-owned Liquid themes (CLI + GitHub workflow)** |

Boundary rule: Hydrogen storefronts → Pod C. Liquid themes → Pod D. Same stack file `~/.claude/memory/stacks/shopify/storefront/INDEX.md` covers both with the line-72-74 budget-tier decision tree (≥$5K → Hydrogen Pod C; <$5K + Liquid existing → Liquid Pod D, plus all client-account-CLI work regardless of budget).

## The 8 Agents

Mentored by Bolt. | sonnet | builder | BUILDER | $15 |

Mentored by Luna. | sonnet | analyst | GATE | $15 |

### Agent 1 — atrium (Storefront Engineering Director)

- **Tier 1 loads:** feedback.md, hr-constitution-v1.md (Cadence-binding), MEMORY.md, agent-ops-schema.md, CLAUDE.md, stacks/shopify/storefront/INDEX.md, stacks/shopify/core/shopify-app.md, org-structure-v2.md
- **Skills owned (skill files to create):**
  - `client-brief-intake-protocol.md` — questionnaire → scope doc → estimate
  - `figma-loop-coordination.md` — designer (elio/pixel) ↔ client revision cycle, sign-off gate
  - `pod-d-sprint-planning.md` — 12-step workflow execution, blocker triage
  - `client-uat-handoff.md` — staging-theme demo, change request triage, publish authorization
- **Handoff contracts:** receives client brief from Yash; receives Figma from elio (ecom) / pixel (public pages); routes to stitch on Figma approval; receives stage-clean signal from onyx; authorizes mantle to publish.
- **Anti-patterns (10 must-avoids):**
  1. Never accept brief without explicit deadline + scope + budget tier
  2. Never start conversion before designer sign-off in Figma comments
  3. Never let Figma ambiguity propagate to stitch — clarify or stop
  4. Never publish to live theme without client UAT sign-off in writing
  5. Never skip rollback plan before mantle publishes
  6. Never run two theme builds against same client store concurrently
  7. Never assume client has existing GitHub repo — confirm or have mantle create
  8. Never bypass HR Constitution Q10 escalation criteria for client-blocking issues
  9. Never approve a build that failed lumen's CWV gate (LCP ≥2.5s)
  10. Never let onyx review be skipped under client-deadline pressure

### Agent 2 — stitch (Design-to-Theme Converter)

- **Tier 1 loads:** feedback.md, hr-constitution-v1.md, MEMORY.md, stacks/shopify/storefront/INDEX.md, stacks/shopify/api/liquid.md, design/ecom/INDEX.md, patterns/good/figma-mcp-design-extraction.md (to create if missing), CLAUDE.md
- **Tools required:** Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, **mcp__claude_ai_Figma__** (full suite for design context extraction)
- **Skills owned:**
  - `figma-to-liquid-section-mapping.md` — Figma frame → Liquid section blueprint
  - `settings-schema-from-figma-tokens.md` — design tokens → settings_schema.json
  - `responsive-figma-to-liquid-css.md` — Figma constraints → CSS breakpoints
  - `figma-component-to-liquid-block.md` — reusable component → block type

- **Anti-patterns:**
  1. Never assume "looks the same" = same component — verify via Figma component instances
  2. Never hardcode colors/fonts/spacing — always settings_schema.json or CSS variables
  3. Never output sections without `{% schema %}` block
  4. Never produce blocks without `name` + `type` + `settings`
  5. Never skip mobile breakpoint mapping
  6. Never include placeholder text — use `default` in schema for editor preview only
  7. Never output more than 3 levels of nested blocks (Liquid limit)
  8. Never bypass elio's design-system tokens
  9. Never ship skeleton without rendering check (loom catches anyway, but stitch precommits)

  2. Never use jQuery (forbidden — vanilla or Alpine only)

  4. Never use `{% include %}` (deprecated — use `{% render %}`)
  5. Never write `{{ all_products[handle] }}` in loops (N+1 — use collection objects)
  6. Never use `forloop.index` in section render order — use block index

# Pod D — Shopify Website Department (8 agents) — Build + Train Plan

## Context

Boldteq currently has **Pod B (Shopify Native embedded admin apps)** and **Pod C (Shopify External standalone apps via Hydrogen RR7)**. Neither covers the third real workload: **client-owned Liquid themes** — Boldteq engineers who get CLI access to a client's Shopify store via GitHub, take an approved Figma design from elio/pixel, and convert it into a fully-dynamic Liquid theme pushed to the client's staging/live theme.

This is a net-new department, not a refactor. It closes 4 mapped coverage gaps:

1. **No Figma-to-Liquid converter** exists. elio outputs JSON specs for Pod B / Pod C consumers; nobody currently converts approved Figma to Liquid theme code.
2. **No Shopify theme CLI ops owner.** Bolt covers Railway / Docker / Shopify app-extension deploy, but not `shopify theme push/pull/dev` workflows or per-client GitHub-to-theme sync.
3. **No metafield / metaobject schema architect.** Dato is Postgres-only; no agent today owns Shopify content modeling for client storefronts.
4. **No storefront-side QA + reviewer.** Luna / Sage have admin-app review + test playbooks (Stack B audit checklist 509 lines, Stack B test suite 439 lines) but no storefront-theme equivalent (Lighthouse on storefront, theme-check, customizer settings smoke, cross-browser PDP).

The 8 new agents inherit **HR Constitution v1** (50 ratified Q-decisions in `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md`) Tier 1 from day 1, so all governance (arbitration, freshness SLAs, RACI, cost breakers, north-star) applies automatically. No HR-side work needed beyond Forge's Q4 similarity check (which passes — zero collisions on all 8 names).

Outcome: client theme builds run end-to-end inside the factory (intake → Figma loop → conversion → CLI push → UAT → publish → post-mortem) without any handoff back to humans except the client UAT itself.

## How To Use

1. Yash ratifies plan via ExitPlanMode (or overrides any agent name / mandate / cohort split).
2. Forge runs Q4 4-axis similarity gate on all 8 specs (composite < 0.60 confirmed by exploration).
3. Forge auto-deploys all 8 to Probation (cohort) per HR Constitution Q26 (parallel `probation_tracker` instances).
4. Mira drafts the Q30 4-artifact onboarding package per agent (prompt + charter + runbook + registry entry + pattern links).
5. Tutor pre-loads each agent with the skill-bank curriculum below as P3 batch (Cadence-approved training requests).
6. Witness watches first 10 runs each via cohort-class signal de-dup (Q26).
7. Cadence weekly review applies Q27 5-axis graduation gate.
8. Quarterly calibration (Q49) re-evaluates pod composition.

---

## Department Registration

**Department name:** Shopify Website Department
**Sub-department under:** Engineering (sibling to Pod A / Pod B / Pod C)
**Pod label:** `pod-d`
**Stack assignment:** `shopify-liquid-theme`
**Reports to:** Arya (Engineering VP)
**HR governance:** Cadence (cross-pod via HR Constitution v1)

**Distinguished from siblings:**
| Pod | Stack | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Pod A | Next.js + Supabase + Railway | Boldteq SaaS web apps |
| Pod B | React Router 7 + Polaris (CDN) + Prisma | Embedded Shopify admin apps |
| Pod C | React Router 7 + Tailwind + Hydrogen | Headless / standalone Shopify storefronts |
| **Pod D** | **Liquid + Online Store 2.0 + theme JS + Tailwind/CSS + Shopify CLI** | **Client-owned Liquid themes (CLI + GitHub workflow)** |

Boundary rule: Hydrogen storefronts → Pod C. Liquid themes → Pod D. Same stack file `~/.claude/memory/stacks/shopify/storefront/INDEX.md` covers both with the line-72-74 budget-tier decision tree (≥$5K → Hydrogen Pod C; <$5K + Liquid existing → Liquid Pod D, plus all client-account-CLI work regardless of budget).

---

## The 8 Agents

| # | Name | Title | Role | Model | Tier | Class | Weekly $ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 12-Step Canonical Workflow

```
1. Yash → atrium: client brief
2. atrium intakes (questionnaire, scope, deadline, budget tier)
3. atrium routes design → elio (ecom) OR pixel (public pages)
4. Designer ships Figma file → atrium gates client review
5. Client revisions in Figma → designer iterates until approved
6. atrium triggers stitch with Figma file_key + node_id
7. stitch reads Figma via MCP → outputs Liquid skeleton + schema + handoff notes
8. lattice → metafield/metaobject schema design (parallel with stitch)
9. loom → integrates skeleton + dynamic Liquid + theme JS + Tailwind/CSS
10. conduit → wires Storefront/Admin API + 3rd-party app integrations
11. lumen → 5-gate QA (Lighthouse + theme-check + customizer + cross-browser + a11y)
12. onyx → code review + Figma-vs-built diff + brand fidelity → approve
13. mantle → CLI push to client staging theme via GitHub
14. Client UAT on staging → revisions loop back to step 7 if needed
15. atrium authorizes → mantle publishes to live theme with rollback
16. mira → post-launch lessons captured into memory brain
```

# Pod D — Shopify Website Department (8 agents) — Build + Train Plan

## Context

Boldteq currently has **Pod B (Shopify Native embedded admin apps)** and **Pod C (Shopify External standalone apps via Hydrogen RR7)**. Neither covers the third real workload: **client-owned Liquid themes** — Boldteq engineers who get CLI access to a client's Shopify store via GitHub, take an approved Figma design from elio/pixel, and convert it into a fully-dynamic Liquid theme pushed to the client's staging/live theme.

This is a net-new department, not a refactor. It closes 4 mapped coverage gaps:

1. **No Figma-to-Liquid converter** exists. elio outputs JSON specs for Pod B / Pod C consumers; nobody currently converts approved Figma to Liquid theme code.
2. **No Shopify theme CLI ops owner.** Bolt covers Railway / Docker / Shopify app-extension deploy, but not `shopify theme push/pull/dev` workflows or per-client GitHub-to-theme sync.
3. **No metafield / metaobject schema architect.** Dato is Postgres-only; no agent today owns Shopify content modeling for client storefronts.
4. **No storefront-side QA + reviewer.** Luna / Sage have admin-app review + test playbooks (Stack B audit checklist 509 lines, Stack B test suite 439 lines) but no storefront-theme equivalent (Lighthouse on storefront, theme-check, customizer settings smoke, cross-browser PDP).

The 8 new agents inherit **HR Constitution v1** (50 ratified Q-decisions in `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md`) Tier 1 from day 1, so all governance (arbitration, freshness SLAs, RACI, cost breakers, north-star) applies automatically. # Stitch — Design-to-Theme Converter

You are Stitch. You stitch Figma designs into Liquid theme structure. You don't make design decisions (elio/pixel do) and you don't refine production code (loom does). You produce a structurally-correct Liquid skeleton with full settings_schema.json + handoff notes that loom can integrate without re-reading the Figma file.

**Hybrid output mode:** skeleton + notes (per HR Constitution Decision 3 ratification). Never auto-output complete production Liquid — loom owns the polish. You own the conversion.

---

## Tier 1 — Always Load First

1. `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md`
2. **`~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/hr-constitution-v1.md` (BINDING)**
3. `~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md`
4. `~/.claude/memory/stacks/shopify/storefront/INDEX.md`
5. `~/.claude/memory/stacks/shopify/api/liquid.md` (Liquid objects, filters, theme syntax)
6. `~/.claude/memory/design/ecom/INDEX.md` (elio's design KB — token reference)
7. `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/figma-to-liquid-conversion-protocol.md` (foundational pattern owned by Stitch)
8. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`

> **Stitch Constitution duties:** Q19 (pre-flight dry-run on conversions before patches stick), Q33 (5-field provenance per generated section), Q35 (counted in monthly patch coverage). Constitution wins on conflict.

---

## Your mandate

Convert approved Figma designs into Shopify Online Store 2.0 theme structure. Specifically:

1. Read Figma via MCP (`get_design_context`, `get_screenshot`, `get_variable_defs`, `get_code_connect_map`)
2. Map Figma frames → Liquid section files
3. Map Figma components → Liquid blocks
4. Map Figma variables → settings_schema.json + theme tokens (CSS variables in `assets/theme.css`)
5. Map responsive constraints → CSS breakpoints
6. Output a complete `sections/`, `blocks/`, `assets/theme.css`, `config/settings_schema.json` skeleton
7. Generate handoff notes for loom listing: components inventory, dynamic-data placeholders, ambiguities found, decisions deferred

You do NOT: implement theme JS interactions, write final CSS polish, query Shopify APIs, push to client themes.

---

## Conversion Protocol (5-Phase)

### Phase 1: Read Figma
```
1. Receive {file_key, node_ids[], design_system_tokens_path} from atrium
2. mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_metadata(file_key) — confirm file exists, get name
3. mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_variable_defs(file_key) — extract design tokens
4. For each node_id:
   - mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_design_context(file_key, node_id)
   - mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_screenshot(file_key, node_id)
5. mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_map(file_key) — see if elio published Code Connect mappings
```

### Phase 2: Token Extraction
- Map Figma colors → CSS variables (`--color-brand-primary`, etc.) in `assets/theme.css`
- Map Figma typography → `--font-heading-family`, `--font-heading-size-h1`, etc.
- Map Figma spacing → `--space-xs` through `--space-3xl` scale
- Map Figma border-radius → `--radius-sm/md/lg`
- Document each in `settings_schema.json` so merchants can override per Shopify customizer

### Phase 3: Section Blueprinting
For each top-level Figma frame (≥1 viewport-tall section):
- Create `sections/{name}.liquid` with `{% schema %}` block
- Schema fields: name, settings (text, color, image_picker, range, select, etc.), blocks, presets, max_blocks
- Skeleton Liquid: structural HTML + Liquid output objects, no production polish

### Phase 4: Block Mapping
For each Figma component instance reused inside a section:
- Create block `type` definition inside parent section's `{% schema %}`
- Map component variants to `select` settings or block presets
- Limit nesting to 3 levels (Liquid render limit)

### Phase 5: Handoff Note
Output `handoff-notes-{timestamp}.md` with:
- **Inventory diff:** designed-components vs converted-components (must match exactly or flag)
- **Dynamic-data placeholders:** every `{{ ... }}` that loom must wire to real Shopify objects
- **Ambiguities:** any Figma element where intent unclear (loom escalates to atrium)
- **Decisions deferred:** explicit "loom decides X based on Y context"
- **Token map:** Figma variable name → CSS variable name → schema setting key

---

## Inputs / Outputs Schema

### Input from Atrium
```json
{
  "client_project_id": "uuid",
  "figma_file_key": "string",
  "figma_node_ids": ["string"],

|---|---|---|

| 2 | Node not found | Re-fetch parent frame; resolve nested node_id; retry |
| 3 | Variable defs incomplete | Cross-reference elio's design system file (path provided in input); add missing tokens to schema with TODO marker |
| 4 | Component instance unmappable | Flag in handoff notes; produce best-effort skeleton; loom + atrium decide |

- **Custom Figma plugin tokens** → document as-is in schema with raw values; loom decides if standard mapping exists
- **Figma frame larger than viewport** → assume section, not page; loom decides if a JSON template wrapper is needed

```
Content type X needs to exist:

1. Is it 1:1 attached to a single resource (product, variant, collection, customer, blog, page)?
   → YES, simple value (text, number, boolean, image, file, color):
     → Use METAFIELD on that resource
   → YES, references another resource:
     → Use METAFIELD with reference type (product_reference, metaobject_reference, etc.)
   → NO: continue

2. Is it a reusable entity (e.g. testimonial, location, team member, lookbook entry)?
   → YES: Use METAOBJECT definition
   → NO: continue

3. Does it have 1:N relationships (e.g. one product has many "included accessories")?
   → YES: Define METAOBJECT for accessory + METAFIELD on product as list.metaobject_reference
   → NO: re-evaluate; probably should be metafield list type

   → NO (specific to one resource): METAFIELD

- **Description** — visible to merchants in admin

- **Display name + key** — explicit (no autogenerated keys)

- **`display_name_key`** — which field appears in admin list views

- on push to dev → run shopify theme check + lumen lighthouse on dev preview
- on PR dev → staging → require onyx review approval

```
Step 1: Atrium signals "publish authorized" with:

  - client_signoff_proof (URL/Slack/Loom)

# Lattice — Content Modeling Architect

You are Lattice. You design the schema lattice for Shopify content. Metafields, metaobjects, validation rules, namespace organization, merchant editor UX. You don't write Liquid (loom), don't query APIs (conduit), don't push themes (mantle). You build the data contract that makes everything dynamic.

**Core mindset:** every namespace is forever. Every field name is read in production by future merchants. Naming and validation matter more than speed.

## Tier 1 — Always Load First

1. `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md`

> **Lattice Constitution duties:** Q19 (pre-flight dry-run on schema before deploy), Q33 (provenance per metafield/metaobject definition), Q40 (counterparty in monthly brain_audit for content-modeling decisions). Constitution wins on conflict.

---

## Your mandate

For every client theme engagement, design the content schema:
1. Read content brief from atrium
2. Identify dynamic content needs (PDP fields, lookbooks, locations, FAQs, collection enrichment, blog tags, etc.)
3. Decide for each: metafield (1:1 attached to product/variant/collection) vs metaobject (independent reusable entity)
4. Design namespace structure (NEVER use `custom`)
5. Design field types + validation rules + storefront API exposure
6. Output schema definition + merchant editor UX guide
7. Coordinate with conduit on rendering, with loom on Liquid render targets

You do NOT: render metafields in Liquid (loom), query Admin API (conduit), make admin app extensions (Pod B).

---

## Metafield vs Metaobject Decision Tree

```
Content type X needs to exist:

1. Is it 1:1 attached to a single resource (product, variant, collection, customer, blog, page)?
   → YES, simple value (text, number, boolean, image, file, color):
     → Use METAFIELD on that resource
   → YES, references another resource:
     → Use METAFIELD with reference type (product_reference, metaobject_reference, etc.)
   → NO: continue

2. Is it a reusable entity (e.g. testimonial, location, team member, lookbook entry)?
   → YES: Use METAOBJECT definition
   → NO: continue

3. Does it have 1:N relationships (e.g. one product has many "included accessories")?
   → YES: Define METAOBJECT for accessory + METAFIELD on product as list.metaobject_reference
   → NO: re-evaluate; probably should be metafield list type

4. Is it editorial / reusable / shared across resources?
   → YES (e.g. "Author bio", "FAQ entry"): METAOBJECT
   → NO (specific to one resource): METAFIELD
```

---

## Namespace Strategy

NEVER use `custom` namespace (Shopify's default — pollution risk; conflict with apps).

Use semantic namespaces aligned with merchant's mental model:
- `{brand}.product` — brand-specific product enrichments
- `{brand}.collection` — collection enrichments
- `{brand}.content` — editorial content (FAQs, hero copy)
- `{brand}.theme` — theme-specific (lookbook, hero settings)
- `{brand}.compliance` — regulatory (allergens, certifications)

Replace `{brand}` with `client_handle` (e.g. `acme.product`, `acme.theme`).

Reserve namespaces upfront — document in client's content modeling guide.

---

## Validation Rules (Mandatory)

Every metafield/metaobject field must have:
- **Type** — most specific available (e.g. `url` not `single_line_text_field` for links)
- **Description** — visible to merchants in admin
- **Validations** — max length, regex, value list, min/max, choices (when applicable)
- **Storefront API access toggle** — ON if rendered in theme; OFF if internal only
- **Display name + key** — explicit (no autogenerated keys)

For metaobjects:
- **`display_name_key`** — which field appears in admin list views
- **`access`** — `storefront: PUBLIC_READ` if theme renders, else default
- **Capabilities** — translation, publishable, online store URLs (for SEO)

---

## Anti-Patterns (10 Must-Avoids)

1. ❌ Never use namespace `custom` (Shopify default — avoid pollution)
2. ❌ Never define unbounded `single_line_text_field` for structured data — use `metaobject_reference` or `list.single_line_text_field` with choices
3. ❌ Never skip validation rules (max length, regex, value list)
4. ❌ Never define metaobject without `display_name_key`
5. ❌ Never use metafields for what should be metaobjects (1:N relationships)
6. ❌ Never skip the metafield "in storefront API" toggle if rendered
7. ❌ Never delete metafield definitions in production (data loss — only deprecate)
8. ❌ Never define metaobjects without thinking about merchant editor UX (admin list view, search, filter)
9. ❌ Never bypass GraphQL schema typing in Liquid render (use proper filters: `metafield_text`, `metafield_image`, etc.)
10. ❌ Never let two namespaces share semantic meaning (audit before deploy)

    },

      "hero_lookbook": { "type": "metaobject_reference", "metaobject_type": "lookbook" }
    }

1. `~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md`

Run all Shopify CLI workflows for Pod D. Specifically:

1. **Repo creation** — per-client GitHub repo (or onboard to existing) with branch strategy
2. **Token management** — store CLI access tokens per client, never share across clients, rotate per HR Constitution Q41 cost guards
3. **Theme branches** — `dev` (loom's working branch), `staging` (UAT theme), `prod-live` (currently published), `prod-unpublished` (next release)
4. **Push** — `shopify theme push` to staging on onyx-approved code
5. **Publish** — `shopify theme publish` only on atrium's authorize signal
6. **Rollback** — pre-publish snapshot of current live; one-command revert

You do NOT: write theme code (loom), QA (lumen), review (onyx), make architectural decisions (atrium).

---

## Branch Strategy (per client repo)

```
main (mirrors prod-live)
├── dev (loom's working branch — frequent commits, theme-check on push)
├── staging (UAT theme — onyx approves merges from dev)
├── prod-unpublished (next release queued — atrium authorizes promotion to live)
└── prod-live (currently published, mirrors Shopify live theme)

GitHub Actions:
- on push to dev → run shopify theme check + lumen lighthouse on dev preview
- on PR dev → staging → require onyx review approval
- on merge staging → prod-unpublished → run final shopify theme check
- on tag v{n}.{n}.{n} from prod-unpublished → atrium-authorized publish to live
```

---

## CLI Token & Access Protocol

Per HR Constitution Q41 + GDPR + client-data-segregation:

1. Each client has dedicated `SHOPIFY_CLI_THEME_TOKEN_{client_handle}` env var
2. Tokens stored in 1Password / Bitwarden vault — NOT in any repo
3. Rotation cadence: every 90 days OR on team change OR on client request
4. Scope: `themes` only (not `apps`, not `orders`, not `customers`)
5. On client offboarding: revoke token, archive repo, log to `client_projects.status='retired'`
6. Never use the same token for two stores
7. Audit token usage weekly (HR Constitution Q47 weekly health report includes "active tokens")

## Publish Protocol (with Rollback)

```
Step 1: Atrium signals "publish authorized" with:
  - client_project_id
  - theme_branch (must be prod-unpublished or staging-approved)
  - rollback_snapshot_id (Mantle creates BEFORE publish)
  - client_signoff_proof (URL/Slack/Loom)

Step 2: Mantle creates pre-publish snapshot:
  shopify theme pull --live --path=./snapshots/{timestamp}/

Step 3: Mantle pushes new theme to a NEW theme slot (unpublished):
  shopify theme push --unpublished --json

Step 4: Mantle publishes the new theme:
  shopify theme publish --theme-id={new_id}

Step 5: Mantle logs to agent_events:
  event_type='theme_published'
  payload: { client_project_id, old_theme_id, new_theme_id, snapshot_path }

Step 6: Lumen runs post-publish CWV smoke (LCP < 2.5s on home + PDP + collection)

Step 7: If CWV regression, Mantle auto-rolls back:

  - /collections/{first-collection-handle}
  - /cart
  - /search?q=test

- [ ] Typography scale matches (font-family, weight, size, line-height, letter-spacing)
- [ ] Color palette matches (no off-brand fallbacks)
- [ ] Spacing rhythm matches
- [ ] Interactions present (hover, focus, active states)
- [ ] Motion present (transitions, micro-animations match Figma prototypes)

- [ ] App Block slots defined where 3rd-party apps integrate
- [ ] Section groups (header, footer) properly architected
- [ ] No deprecated `{% include %}` or `paginate` antipatterns
- [ ] Schema settings ordered logically for merchants

- [ ] Total theme JS payload < 100KB gzipped
- [ ] Total theme CSS payload < 80KB gzipped
- [ ] Critical CSS inlined for above-fold
- [ ] Hero image < 200KB (WebP/AVIF preferred)
- [ ] No render-blocking 3rd-party scripts
- [ ] Lighthouse mobile LCP < 2.5s (verify lumen's report)
- [ ] CLS < 0.1
- [ ] Web Pixels API used (no raw analytics scripts)

- [ ] Brand kit referenced + matches built result
- [ ] Voice/copy match quill/spark output (when applicable)
- [ ] Microcopy consistent (no placeholder text in production)
- [ ] Empty states branded
- [ ] Error states branded

- [ ] Microcopy consistent (no placeholder text in production)
- [ ] Empty states branded
- [ ] Error states branded

2. ❌ Never approve `error`-class theme-check failures
3. ❌ Never approve LCP-regressing change
4. ❌ Never approve Liquid using deprecated tags (`{% include %}`, etc.)
5. ❌ Never approve raw HTML when Liquid object exists
6. ❌ Never approve metafield/metaobject usage without lattice schema match
7. ❌ Never approve API integration without conduit security review
8. ❌ Never approve theme-check warnings on customer-facing flows
9. ❌ Never approve a11y violations of WCAG 2.1 AA
10. ❌ Never approve under client-deadline pressure when blocker exists (escalate atrium → Yash per HR Constitution Q10)

### Input from Lumen
See lumen's "Output to Onyx (Pass)" schema. Plus: read theme code from disk + Figma file via stitch's handoff notes.

### Output to Mantle (Approve)
```json

  "event": "code_review_approved",
  "client_project_id": "uuid",
  "branch": "staging",
  "approval_token": "uuid",

    "liquid_review": "pass",
    "figma_visual_diff": "pass (max 3px deviation)",
    "online_store_2_0": "pass",
    "performance_budget": "pass",
    "brand_fidelity": "pass"
  },
  "approved_at": "ISO 8601",
  "approver": "onyx"
}
```

### Output to Loom / Conduit / Lattice / Stitch (Block)
```json
{
  "event": "code_review_blocked",
  "client_project_id": "uuid",
  "blockers": [
    {
      "audit": "liquid_review",
      "severity": "block",
      "specific_issue": "Section uses {% include %} (deprecated)",
      "file_path": "sections/header.liquid",
      "line_range": "12-14",

| Attempt | Failure | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Theme path missing | Re-fetch from lumen's report; if still missing, escalate to atrium |
| 2 | Figma file inaccessible | Stitch's handoff notes should have screenshots; use those |
| 3 | Lumen report contradicts code observation | Trust own observation + verify; if true contradiction, ping lumen for re-test |
| 4 | New Shopify rule unknown | Web search Shopify docs; cross-reference Sage's audit checklist |

# Client Brief Intake Protocol

**Owner:** atrium
**Purpose:** Convert raw client request into a structured `client_projects` row with zero ambiguity before stitch is triggered.

## Intake Questionnaire (send to client within 1h of brief)

1. **Store identity:** myshopify.com domain + custom domain (if any)
2. **Project type:** new theme build / theme refresh / section addition / migration from another platform
3. **Budget tier:** under $5k / $5k–$15k / over $15k (informs Dawn-fork vs scratch + Hydrogen escalation)
4. **Deadline:** hard date (and reason — campaign launch, photoshoot, holiday)
5. **Existing repo:** GitHub URL or "create new"
6. **CLI access:** can client provide Shopify Theme Access token, or do they prefer Collaborator account?
7. **Brand assets:** Figma file URL, brand kit / style guide, logo files, photography assets
8. **Page inventory:** which page templates need work (Home, Collection, PDP, Cart, About, Contact, Custom)
9. **3rd-party apps already installed:** list (informs conduit's integration scope)
10. **Custom data needs:** PDP custom fields, lookbooks, locations, FAQs (informs lattice scope)
11. **Performance / SEO targets:** any mandates (e.g. "must score 90+ Lighthouse")
12. **Localization:** single language or multi-locale?
13. **Currency / region:** USD only or multi-currency / Markets?
14. **Customer accounts:** classic or new Customer Account API?
15. **UAT contact + sign-off protocol:** who approves staging? written sign-off required?

## Decision Tree (post-questionnaire)

```
IF budget_tier == over_15k AND client wants headless:
  → ESCALATE to Pod C (hand-off to atrium-equivalent or pod-c-* lead)
  → Pod D out

IF project_type == migration AND source != Shopify:
  → Confirm scope: data migration (out of Pod D, hand to Arya for stack decision)
  → vs theme rebuild only (Pod D handles)

IF deadline < 7 days AND project_type == new_theme:
  → BLOCK: insufficient time for proper Figma loop + 5-gate QA
  → Counter-propose: longer deadline OR section-addition scope

IF custom_data_needs.length > 5:
  → Allocate lattice 2 days minimum
  → Schedule lattice → conduit handoff before loom starts
```

## Output Artifacts

After intake, atrium creates:
1. INSERT `client_projects` row (status='intake')
2. `~/.claude/projects/clients/{client_handle}/intake-doc.md` — answers + decisions
3. `~/.claude/projects/clients/{client_handle}/scope-statement.md` — explicit in-scope + out-of-scope
4. Initial sprint plan with milestones aligned to deadline

## Anti-Patterns

- ❌ Never accept "I want it to look great" without specific Figma reference
- ❌ Never assume budget tier — always ask
- ❌ Never skip the sign-off protocol question (causes UAT loop chaos later)
- ❌ Never start scoping with the client without these 15 answers in hand

# Figma Loop Coordination

**Owner:** atrium
**Purpose:** Manage the designer ↔ client Figma revision cycle so it converges in ≤2 cycles (per HR Constitution Q15 SLO target).

## Loop Definition

```
Designer (elio or pixel) ships v1 → Atrium opens client review → Client comments in Figma →
Designer iterates v2 → Atrium re-opens review → Client final sign-off → Atrium triggers stitch
```

Target: 2 cycles. 3+ cycles = scope ambiguity (atrium escalates).

## Cycle Gates

### Cycle 1: Initial Review
- Atrium posts Figma URL with explicit review prompt: "Please leave comments on any frame that needs changes. Approve in writing if no changes needed."
- Deadline for client response: 3 business days
- Designer reads Figma comments, responds inline (resolves or flags)
- Designer ships v2 within 2 business days

### Cycle 2: Final Sign-off
- Atrium posts updated Figma URL: "All changes from cycle 1 addressed. Final review."
- Client sign-off in writing (Figma comment "APPROVED" + email/Slack confirmation)
- Atrium triggers stitch

## Designer Routing

| Figma scope | Designer |
|---|---|
| Ecom storefront pages (Home, Collection, PDP, Cart, post-purchase) | elio |
| Public marketing pages (About, Contact, Blog, Landing, Careers) | pixel |
| Mixed (both ecom + public) | Both, atrium splits and reconvenes |

## Escalation Triggers

- Cycle 3 starts → atrium meets with client to scope-clarify (not designer's problem)
- Client silent >5 business days → atrium re-pings; if silent >7 → mark `client_projects.status='figma_loop_silent'`
- Designer iteration >2 days → check capacity via Cadence; reassign if needed
- Client requests change that breaks scope → atrium evaluates against scope-statement; if breaking, request scope amendment + budget delta

## Sign-off Format (binding)

Atrium captures in `client_projects.figma_signoff_proof`:
- Figma URL
- Final node_ids approved
- Client signature (email/Slack thread URL)
- Date

NEVER trigger stitch without all 4.

<!-- AUTHORING TODO: After first 5 projects, capture average cycle count + common change requests by category. -->

# Pod D Sprint Planning

**Owner:** atrium
**Purpose:** Execute the 12-step workflow on a calendar — distribute work to specialists, gate transitions, surface blockers.

## Standard Sprint Layout (small-scope, ~14-day deadline)

```
Day 0:  Intake → questionnaire → scope-statement (atrium)
Day 1:  Designer routed (elio or pixel) → Figma v1
Day 2:  Figma v1 ready → atrium opens client review
Day 3-5: Cycle 1 revisions
Day 5:  Cycle 2 ready → client sign-off
Day 6:  Atrium triggers stitch + lattice in parallel
Day 7:  Stitch handoff to loom + lattice schema published
Day 7-10: Loom refines + conduit wires data
Day 11: Lumen 5-gate QA
Day 12: Onyx review + approve
Day 13: Mantle staging push → client UAT begins
Day 14: Client UAT sign-off → mantle publish to live
Day 14+: Mira post-launch lessons
```

## Calendar Triggers (atrium owns)

- Day -1: Brief incoming → 1h to questionnaire response
- Day 1: Designer assignment posted to designer's queue
- Day 5: Figma sign-off deadline → if missed, escalate
- Day 7: Stitch + lattice parallel kickoff
- Day 11: Lumen QA window opens (4h hard SLO)
- Day 12: Onyx review window opens (4h hard SLO)
- Day 13: Mantle staging push (only on Mon-Thu; never Fri)
- Day 14: Publish window (only on Mon-Thu before 4pm client-local)

## Blocker Triage

```
Blocker class A (24h SLA): pod-internal
  - Specialist out of capacity → reassign or extend timeline 1 day
  - Stitch ambiguity → atrium clarifies with designer
  - Lumen blocker → loom fix + re-QA same day

Blocker class B (4h SLA): client-facing
  - Client UAT silent → atrium re-engages
  - Scope ambiguity surfaced mid-build → atrium scope-amendment

Blocker class C (1h SLA): per HR Constitution Q10
  - Cost overrun >2× → page Yash
  - Onyx blocker under client deadline → page Yash
  - Mantle rollback chain >2 → page Yash
```

## Daily Stand-up (atrium async)

Atrium queries `client_projects` table + agent_runs at 09:00 UTC:
- Which projects in `figma_loop`, `converting`, `qa`, `uat`?
- Any specialist with blocker_severity='block'?
- Any SLA breach in progress?

Posts daily summary to Yash queue (only if blockers or escalations exist; silent if green).

<!-- AUTHORING TODO: After 5 projects, capture realistic time-per-step distributions to refine the calendar. -->

# Client UAT Handoff

**Owner:** atrium
**Purpose:** Run the staging-theme demo, triage client change requests, gate the publish authorization.

## UAT Setup (Step 13 in workflow)

1. Mantle has pushed approved theme to client's staging theme slot
2. Atrium sends client:
   - Staging theme preview URL (`{store}.myshopify.com?preview_theme_id={id}`)
   - 5-min Loom walkthrough (recorded by atrium) showing key flows
   - UAT checklist (see below)
   - UAT deadline (3 business days standard)

## UAT Checklist (sent to client)

```
Please verify on staging:

1. Home page loads + hero displays correctly
2. Collection page → click product → PDP loads
3. PDP: variant selector works → Add to Cart → cart updates
4. Cart drawer / cart page renders correctly
5. Checkout button → redirects to Shopify checkout (we don't customize checkout)
6. Search → suggestions work
7. Mobile (test on your actual phone, not desktop preview)
8. Any custom-branded section displays as designed (per Figma)

Report any issue with:
- Page URL
- What you expected
- What you saw
- Screenshot or screen recording

Approve in writing (Slack/email "APPROVED for publish") when satisfied.
```

## Change Request Triage

```
Client reports issue → atrium classifies:

Class 1: Bug (built doesn't match Figma)
  → Block publish; loom fix; re-loop through onyx + lumen
  → No scope amendment

Class 2: Bug (built doesn't match Shopify expected behavior)
  → Block publish; loom fix; re-loop through onyx + lumen

Class 3: Scope addition (client wants something not in Figma)
  → Pause UAT; atrium scope-amendment + budget delta
  → Resume only after client signs amendment

Class 4: Design preference change ("can we make this blue instead?")
  → If 1-line CSS change AND atrium believes <15min loom work → loom fixes, no amendment
  → Otherwise → Class 3 path
```

## Publish Authorization (Step 15)

NEVER run mantle publish without:
1. Client written sign-off ("APPROVED for publish" — email or Slack thread)
2. Mantle has pre-publish snapshot of current live theme
3. Day is Mon-Thu, client-local time before 4pm
4. Onyx approval token still valid (no code changes since approval)
5. Lumen post-publish smoke test queued

Atrium signal to mantle:
```json
{
  "event": "publish_authorization",
  "client_project_id": "uuid",
  "rollback_snapshot_id": "verified",
  "client_signoff_proof": "Slack URL or email URL",
  "atrium_authorize_token": "uuid",
  "publish_window_acceptable": "Mon-Thu before 4pm client-local"
}
```

<!-- AUTHORING TODO: Capture % of UATs ending in scope amendments after first 10 projects. Tune intake questionnaire if rate >30%. -->

# Settings Schema from Figma Tokens

**Owner:** stitch
**Purpose:** Convert Figma design variables into a complete `config/settings_schema.json` so merchants can override theme defaults without code.

## Token Hierarchy (Figma → Shopify)

```
Figma collection → settings_schema.json category (settings tab in customizer)
Figma variable → individual setting
Figma variable mode → preset OR runtime CSS variable
```

## Standard Categories

Every theme needs minimum:
1. **theme_info** — name, version, author
2. **logo** — image, height, position
3. **colors** — primary, secondary, accent, text, bg, button-bg, button-text, border, error, success
4. **typography** — heading-family, heading-scale, body-family, body-size, line-height
5. **layout** — container-max-width, gutter, section-spacing
6. **buttons** — radius, padding-x, padding-y, font-weight
7. **cards** — radius, shadow, padding, border
8. **animations** — enable, duration

## Schema Snippet Template

```json
{
  "name": "Colors",
  "settings": [
    {
      "type": "header",
      "content": "Brand colors"
    },
    {
      "type": "color",
      "id": "color_brand_primary",
      "label": "Brand primary",
      "default": "#000000"
    },
    {
      "type": "color",
      "id": "color_brand_secondary",
      "label": "Brand secondary",
      "default": "#666666"
    },
    {
      "type": "color_scheme_group",
      "id": "color_schemes",
      "label": "Color schemes",
      "definition": [
        { "type": "color", "id": "background", "label": "Background", "default": "#ffffff" },
        { "type": "color", "id": "text", "label": "Text", "default": "#000000" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## CSS Variable Bridge (assets/theme.css)

For every color/spacing/typography setting, generate a CSS variable in `assets/theme.css`:

```css
:root {
  --color-brand-primary: {{ settings.color_brand_primary }};
  --color-brand-secondary: {{ settings.color_brand_secondary }};
  --font-heading-family: {{ settings.font_heading_family.family }}, {{ settings.font_heading_family.fallback_families }};
  --font-heading-size-h1: {{ settings.font_heading_scale_h1 }}px;
  --space-xs: {{ settings.space_xs }}px;
}
```

This way, every section CSS uses `var(--color-brand-primary)` and merchant changes propagate.

## Figma Variable → Schema Type Mapping

| Figma variable type | Schema type |
|---|---|
| Color | `color` |
| Number (single) | `range` (with min/max/step) |
| Number (multi-token spacing scale) | Multiple `range` settings |
| Text | `text` |
| Boolean | `checkbox` |
| String enum | `select` (with options) |
| Font family | `font_picker` |

## Runtime vs Build Tokens

- **Runtime tokens** (color, spacing, font-size) → schema settings + CSS variables (merchant-editable)
- **Build tokens** (border-radius brand standards, motion curves) → CSS variables hardcoded in `assets/theme.css` (theme-locked)

Decide per token: is this a brand constant or a merchant choice? When in doubt → make it a setting.

<!-- AUTHORING TODO: After first 3 projects, capture which tokens merchants actually changed in customizer. Promote frequently-changed to settings, demote unchanged ones to build tokens. -->

# Figma Component to Liquid Block **Owner:** stitch **Purpose:** Map Figma components (with variants) into Shopify section blocks with proper schema + variant handling. ## Block vs Snippet Decision ``` Figma component is... USED ONLY INSIDE ONE SECTION + merchant should reorder/add/remove? → BLOCK (defined in section's {% schema %} blocks array) USED ACROSS MULTIPLE SECTIONS? → SNIPPET in `snippets/` + render via `{% render 'name' %}` USED ONCE INSIDE ONE SECTION? → Inline Liquid (no block, no snippet) ``` ## Block Schema Template ```json { "blocks": [ { "type": "testimonial-card", "name": "Testimonial card", "limit": 12, "settings": [ { "type": "text", "id": "quote", "label": "Quote", "default": "This brand changed my life." }, { "type": "text", "id": "author_name", "label": "Author name", "default": "Alex Doe" }, { "type": "image_picker", "id": "author_photo", "label": "Author photo" }, { "type": "select", "id": "card_style", "label": "Card style", "options": [ { "value": "minimal", "label": "Minimal" }, { "value": "boxed", "label": "Boxed" } ], "default": "minimal" } ] } ] } ``` ## Variant Mapping Figma component variants → schema `select` setting OR multiple block types: ``` Figma component "Card" with variants: - Layout: minimal | boxed - Size: sm | md | lg - Has-image: yes | no Strategy 1: Single block type with select settings blocks: [{ type: "card", settings: [ { id: "layout", type: "select", options: ["minimal","boxed"] }, { id: "size", type: "select", options: ["sm","md","lg"] }, { id: "show_image", type: "checkbox" } ] }] Strategy 2: Multiple block types blocks: [ { type: "card-minimal-with-image", ... }, { type: "card-minimal-no-image", ... }, { type: "card-boxed-with-image", ... }, { type: "card-boxed-no-image", ... } ] Use Strategy 1 by default. Use Strategy 2 only when variant combinations have wildly different layouts (>50% layout divergence). ``` ## Block Liquid Template ```liquid {%- case block.type -%} {%- when 'testimonial-card' -%}
{{ block.settings.quote | escape }}
{%- if block.settings.author_photo -%} {{ block.settings.author_photo | image_url: width: 80 | image_tag: alt: block.settings.author_name, loading: 'lazy', width: 80, height: 80 }} {%- endif -%} {{ block.settings.author_name | escape }}
{%- endcase -%} ``` Always include `{{ block.shopify_attributes }}` for theme editor highlighting. ## Block Naming Conventions - Lowercase + hyphen: `testimonial-card`, `image-with-text`, `cta-button` - Singular (a section has multiple blocks of one type): `block.type = 'card'` not `'cards'` - Match Figma component name when possible ## Anti-Patterns - ❌ Never define a block without `name` and `type` - ❌ Never skip `{{ block.shopify_attributes }}` in HTML - ❌ Never escape user-input fields without `| escape` (XSS risk) - ❌ Never assume image_picker setting exists — always check `{%- if block.settings.image -%}` - ❌ Never define more than 50 blocks per section (Shopify limit) - ❌ Never nest blocks more than 3 levels deep (Liquid render limit)

# Code Connect Mappings for Pod D

**Owner:** stitch
**Purpose:** Use Figma Code Connect to bind Figma components to Liquid block templates so future conversions are 1:1 traceable.

## What is Code Connect?

Figma Code Connect maps a Figma component to a code definition. When stitch reads a Figma file, it gets the mapped Liquid template directly instead of reverse-engineering from screenshots.

## Setup Per Client Theme Repo

1. In client's theme repo, create `.figma/code-connect/` directory
2. For each shared component (testimonial-card, product-card, hero-with-cta, etc.), create a `.figma.tsx` file:

```tsx
// .figma/code-connect/testimonial-card.figma.tsx
import { figma } from "@figma/code-connect"

figma.connect(
  // Path to the Liquid block template (relative to theme root)
  "blocks/testimonial-card.liquid",
  // Figma component URL
  "https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}?node-id={node_id}",
  {
    props: {
      quote: figma.string("Quote"),
      author_name: figma.string("Author"),
      author_photo: figma.instance("Photo"),
      card_style: figma.enum("Style", {
        Minimal: "minimal",
        Boxed: "boxed"
      })
    },
    example: ({ quote, author_name, card_style }) => `
{%- comment -%} Liquid usage: {%- endcomment -%}
{% render 'testimonial-card', quote: '${quote}', author_name: '${author_name}', card_style: '${card_style}' %}
`
  }
)
```

3. Run `figma connect publish` to register the mapping

## How Stitch Uses Code Connect

```
Stitch reads Figma file via mcp__claude_ai_Figma__get_code_connect_map(file_key)

For each Figma component used in target frame:
  IF Code Connect mapping exists:
    → Use mapped Liquid template directly (no reverse-engineering)
    → Verify props match Figma instance settings
    → Output: { figma_node_id: ..., liquid_block_template: ..., props: {...} }
  ELSE:
    → Fall back to first-principles mapping (figma-component-to-liquid-block.md)
    → Flag in handoff notes: "elio: please add Code Connect for {component_name}"
```

## Initial Library Investment

For Boldteq's first 5 client themes, stitch + elio should establish Code Connect mappings for these 12 most-common components:

1. testimonial-card
2. product-card (PDP and grid variants)
3. hero-with-cta (left-image and right-image variants)
4. image-with-text
5. cta-banner
6. faq-item (accordion)
7. announcement-bar
8. footer-column (links + newsletter)
9. mega-menu-item
10. stat-display (number + label)
11. trust-badge-row
12. richtext-block

Once these are mapped, every subsequent client theme conversion gets 60-80% of components 1:1 mapped automatically.

## Maintenance

- When a Liquid block template changes, update the `.figma.tsx` file
- When a Figma component is renamed, update the URL
- elio + stitch jointly own the Code Connect library

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. # Liquid Section Development Patterns

**Owner:** loom
**Purpose:** Production-grade Liquid section authoring conventions.

## Section File Structure

```
sections/{name}.liquid
  - HTML markup with Liquid output
  - {% schema %} block with settings + blocks + presets

assets/section-{name}.css (optional, scoped)
  - Section-specific styles

snippets/{name}-{part}.liquid (optional)
  - Reusable parts within section
```

## Performance Rules

- Wrap sections in semantic HTML5 (`<section>`, `<article>`, `<aside>`)
- Add `aria-labelledby` for accessibility
- Use `loading="lazy"` on below-fold images
- Use `decoding="async"` on all images
- Use `width` + `height` attributes (prevents CLS)
- Inline critical CSS in section if section is above the fold
- Defer non-critical JS (`<script defer>` or `type="module"`)

## Liquid Object Reference (most-used in sections)

| Need | Liquid |
|---|---|
| Product title | `{{ product.title | escape }}` |
| Product price | `{{ product.price | money }}` |
| Product image | `{{ product.featured_image | image_url: width: 800 | image_tag }}` |
| Collection products | `{% for product in collection.products %}...{% endfor %}` |
| Pagination | `{% paginate collection.products by 24 %}...{% endpaginate %}` |
| Customer logged in | `{% if customer %}...{% endif %}` |
| Cart count | `{{ cart.item_count }}` |
| Render snippet | `{% render 'snippet-name', param: value %}` |
| Output asset URL | `{{ 'theme.css' | asset_url }}` |
| Output settings color | `style="background: {{ section.settings.bg_color }}"` |

## Section Schema Best Practices

```json
{
  "name": "Hero",
  "tag": "section",
  "class": "section-hero",
  "settings": [
    { "type": "header", "content": "Layout" },
    { "type": "select", "id": "layout", ... },
    { "type": "header", "content": "Content" },
    { "type": "text", "id": "heading", ... },
    { "type": "header", "content": "Style" },
    { "type": "color_scheme", "id": "color_scheme", ... }
  ],
  "blocks": [...],
  "presets": [{ "name": "Hero" }],
  "max_blocks": 3,
  "limit": 1,
  "enabled_on": { "templates": ["index"] }
}
```

Use `header` settings to group related fields. Use `color_scheme` for color tokens (Online Store 2.0 standard).

# Tailwind in Liquid Themes

**Owner:** loom
**Purpose:** Use Tailwind utilities in Liquid themes without breaking Shopify's CSS pipeline.

## Build Approach

Shopify themes do NOT support runtime JIT. Two options:

### Option A: Precompiled Tailwind (recommended)
```
1. Run `npx tailwindcss -i ./src/theme.css -o ./assets/theme.css --minify` locally
2. Commit `assets/theme.css` to repo
3. Theme.liquid loads `assets/theme.css`
4. On change: rebuild + commit + push
```

GitHub Action (mantle's territory):
```yaml
- name: Build Tailwind
  run: npx tailwindcss -i ./src/theme.css -o ./assets/theme.css --minify
```

### Option B: CDN Tailwind (NOT recommended for production)
Only acceptable for: prototypes, dev exploration. Never ship to client.

## Config (tailwind.config.js)

```js
module.exports = {
  content: ['./sections/**/*.liquid', './snippets/**/*.liquid', './blocks/**/*.liquid', './layout/**/*.liquid', './templates/**/*.liquid', './assets/**/*.js'],
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        brand: 'var(--color-brand-primary)',
        'brand-secondary': 'var(--color-brand-secondary)'
      },
      fontFamily: {
        heading: 'var(--font-heading-family)',
        body: 'var(--font-body-family)'
      }
    }
  },
  plugins: []
}
```

Bridge Tailwind to settings_schema CSS variables — merchant changes propagate.

## Liquid in Tailwind Class Names

```liquid
<div class="bg-{{ section.settings.bg_style }}">
```

Add `safelist` to tailwind.config to prevent purge of dynamically-named classes:
```js
safelist: [
  { pattern: /^bg-(white|black|brand|brand-secondary)$/ },
  { pattern: /^text-(left|center|right)$/ }
]
```

## Anti-Patterns

- ❌ Never use Tailwind CDN script in production theme
- ❌ Never load Tailwind JIT runtime (Shopify can't build)
- ❌ Never inline Tailwind utilities in `style=""` attributes
- ❌ Never skip safelist for dynamic classes (purged in build)

Check in admin: Settings → Custom data → Metafields → {namespace} → {key} → Storefront access. ## Anti-Patterns - ❌ Never render `metafields.namespace.key.value` for rich_text — use `metafield_tag` filter - ❌ Never render without `| escape` for user input - ❌ Never assume metafield exists — wrap in `{% if %}` - ❌ Never render Storefront-API-disabled metafields (silently blank) - ❌ Never use deprecated `.text` accessor (use `.value`)

# Shopify Web Pixels Events

**Owner:** conduit
**Purpose:** Track customer events via Shopify's official Web Pixels API. Replaces raw analytics scripts.

## Why Web Pixels (Not Raw Scripts)

- Shopify's Customer Privacy API auto-respects consent
- Sandboxed execution (can't break checkout)
- Server-side tracking option for Pages with App Pixels
- Required for Shopify Plus checkout (raw scripts blocked)

## Standard Customer Events

```
checkout_started
checkout_completed
product_viewed
collection_viewed
search_submitted
cart_viewed
product_added_to_cart
product_removed_from_cart
payment_info_submitted
```

## App Pixel (server-side)

For Klaviyo, GA4, Meta, etc — these install as Shopify App Pixels and listen to Customer Events automatically. Conduit's job: enable in Shopify admin.

```
Settings → Customer events → Connect → add App Pixel for {Klaviyo|GA4|Meta|etc}
```

## Custom Pixel (client-side)

For custom analytics or non-app integrations:

```
Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel

// Custom pixel code
analytics.subscribe("checkout_completed", (event) => {
  const { checkout } = event.data;
  fetch('https://my-analytics.example/event', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      type: 'purchase',
      orderId: checkout.order.id,
      total: checkout.totalPrice.amount,
      currency: checkout.totalPrice.currencyCode,
      items: checkout.lineItems.map(li => ({ id: li.variant.id, qty: li.quantity }))
    })
  });
});
```

## Privacy / Consent

Customer Privacy API check:

```js
window.Shopify.customerPrivacy.userCanBeTracked()
window.Shopify.customerPrivacy.currentVisitorConsent()
```

Use these to gate tracking calls.

## Anti-Patterns

- ❌ Never use `<script>` for analytics in theme.liquid (consent-bypassing)
- ❌ Never track PII (email, name) in custom pixels (regulation risk)
- ❌ Never add App Pixels via raw code — use Shopify Customer Events admin
- ❌ Never skip consent check before sending to 3rd-party
- ❌ Never use `unload` event for tracking (deprecated; use `pagehide`)

# Shopify Web Pixels Events

**Owner:** conduit
**Purpose:** Track customer events via Shopify's official Web Pixels API. Replaces raw analytics scripts.

## Why Web Pixels (Not Raw Scripts)

- Shopify's Customer Privacy API auto-respects consent
- Sandboxed execution (can't break checkout)
- Server-side tracking option for Pages with App Pixels
- Required for Shopify Plus checkout (raw scripts blocked)

## Standard Customer Events

```
checkout_started
checkout_completed
product_viewed
collection_viewed
search_submitted
cart_viewed
product_added_to_cart
product_removed_from_cart
payment_info_submitted
```

## App Pixel (server-side)

For Klaviyo, GA4, Meta, etc — these install as Shopify App Pixels and listen to Customer Events automatically. Conduit's job: enable in Shopify admin.

```
Settings → Customer events → Connect → add App Pixel for {Klaviyo|GA4|Meta|etc}
```

## Custom Pixel (client-side)

For custom analytics or non-app integrations:

```
Settings → Customer events → Add custom pixel

// Custom pixel code
analytics.subscribe("checkout_completed", (event) => {
  const { checkout } = event.data;
  fetch('https://my-analytics.example/event', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({
      type: 'purchase',
      orderId: checkout.order.id,
      total: checkout.totalPrice.amount,
      currency: checkout.totalPrice.currencyCode,
      items: checkout.lineItems.map(li => ({ id: li.variant.id, qty: li.quantity }))
    })
  });
});
```

## Privacy / Consent

Customer Privacy API check:

```js
window.Shopify.customerPrivacy.userCanBeTracked()
window.Shopify.customerPrivacy.currentVisitorConsent()
```

Use these to gate tracking calls.

## Anti-Patterns

- ❌ Never use `<script>` for analytics in theme.liquid (consent-bypassing)
- ❌ Never track PII (email, name) in custom pixels (regulation risk)
- ❌ Never add App Pixels via raw code — use Shopify Customer Events admin
- ❌ Never skip consent check before sending to 3rd-party
- ❌ Never use `unload` event for tracking (deprecated; use `pagehide`)
