63	## Audit Checklist
64	
65	### Audit 1: Liquid Code Review
66	- [ ] No `{% include %}` (use `{% render %}`)
67	- [ ] No raw HTML when Liquid object exists (`<a href="/products">` → `{{ 'products' | link_to_collection }}`)
68	- [ ] No N+1 in loops (`{{ all_products[handle] }}` inside `{% for %}` blocks)
69	- [ ] All sections have `{% schema %}` blocks
70	- [ ] All blocks have `name` + `type` + `settings`
71	- [ ] No hardcoded colors / fonts / spacing (must reference settings or CSS vars)
72	- [ ] Lazy-load attributes on below-fold images (`loading="lazy"`)
73	- [ ] Section dependencies clear (no circular renders)
74	- [ ] Schema max_blocks set sensibly
75	- [ ] `{% liquid %}` blocks for multi-line logic when readability suffers
76	
77	### Audit 2: Figma-vs-Built Visual Diff
78	- [ ] Side-by-side screenshots: Figma frame vs built section
79	- [ ] Pixel diff < 5px on common viewports (375, 768, 1280, 1920)
80	- [ ] Token map verified: every Figma variable → CSS var → schema setting
81	- [ ] Typography scale matches (font-family, weight, size, line-height, letter-spacing)
82	- [ ] Color palette matches (no off-brand fallbacks)
83	- [ ] Spacing rhythm matches
84	- [ ] Interactions present (hover, focus, active states)
85	- [ ] Motion present (transitions, micro-animations match Figma prototypes)
86	
87	### Audit 3: Online Store 2.0
88	- [ ] JSON templates used for all main pages (index, product, collection, page, blog, article)
89	- [ ] Sections support customizer drag-drop
90	- [ ] App Block slots defined where 3rd-party apps integrate
91	- [ ] Section groups (header, footer) properly architected
92	- [ ] No deprecated `{% include %}` or `paginate` antipatterns
93	- [ ] Schema settings ordered logically for merchants
94	
95	### Audit 4: Performance Budget
96	- [ ] Total theme JS payload < 100KB gzipped
97	- [ ] Total theme CSS payload < 80KB gzipped
98	- [ ] Critical CSS inlined for above-fold
99	- [ ] Hero image < 200KB (WebP/AVIF preferred)
100	- [ ] No render-blocking 3rd-party scripts
101	- [ ] Lighthouse mobile LCP < 2.5s (verify lumen's report)
102	- [ ] CLS < 0.1
103	- [ ] Web Pixels API used (no raw analytics scripts)

63	## Metafield vs Metaobject Decision Tree
64	
65	```
66	Content type X needs to exist:
67	
68	1. Is it 1:1 attached to a single resource (product, variant, collection, customer, blog, page)?
69	   → YES, simple value (text, number, boolean, image, file, color):
70	     → Use METAFIELD on that resource
71	   → YES, references another resource:
72	     → Use METAFIELD with reference type (product_reference, metaobject_reference, etc.)
73	   → NO: continue
74	
75	2. Is it a reusable entity (e.g. testimonial, location, team member, lookbook entry)?
76	   → YES: Use METAOBJECT definition
77	   → NO: continue
78	
79	3. Does it have 1:N relationships (e.g. one product has many "included accessories")?
80	   → YES: Define METAOBJECT for accessory + METAFIELD on product as list.metaobject_reference
81	   → NO: re-evaluate; probably should be metafield list type
82	
83	4. Is it editorial / reusable / shared across resources?
84	   → YES (e.g. "Author bio", "FAQ entry"): METAOBJECT
85	   → NO (specific to one resource): METAFIELD
86	```

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- test: /test — Intelligent Test Runner
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".

**1. Data Grouping Field:** **`department`** (primary grouping) + **`subDepartment`** (secondary grouping within dept)

- Line 406: `return m.subDepartment === sd.id` (matches agents to sub-dept buckets)

**2. "Unassigned" Logic (Lines 438–461):**
- Agents land here if they're NOT in any department's `members` list
- `buildColumnMembers()` filters by `department === deptId` (line 354)
- Any agent whose `department` ≠ a defined dept ID gets excluded from normal columns
- Then collected as residual: `const unassigned = allNodes.filter(n => !renderedIds.has(n.id))`
- These become synthetic "Unassigned" column (grey, no brand color)

**3. "Other" Fallback (Line 502):**
- Within a dense department (≥8 members, ≥2 sub-depts), agents who have `department=engineering` BUT `subDepartment` doesn't match ANY configured sub-dept

- These land in `{ label: 'Other', members: ungrouped, subDeptId: 'engineering-other' }`

- **Sub-department labels:** Read from `departments.json` → `subDepartments[].label` (line 396–400)
- **Department list & order:** Dynamic from server (line 413)

# Dynamic Org-Chart Assignment Workflow — Build Plan

## Context

The Boldteq Polyglot org-chart UI (`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx`) currently breaks the assignment workflow in three ways:

1. **Pod dropdown is hardcoded** to 3 options (`saas`, `shopify-app`, `shopify-web`) at OrgChart.tsx:1758–1765. Adding a new team (like the just-created `shopify-website-team` for Liquid themes) requires editing TSX code.
2. **Card grouping is brittle.** When `subDepartment` on an agent doesn't match an entry in `departments.json → engineering.subDepartments`, the agent lands in synthetic "Other" or "Unassigned" columns. Right now 7 of 8 Shopify Website Team agents are visible in "Unassigned" / "Other" because the registry.json + departments.json drift wasn't reseeded into the running server.
3. **No card-level visual controls.** Card label, color, icon, order can't be edited from the UI — they're either hardcoded constants in TSX or derived from incomplete `departments.json` entries.

The user wants a **fully dynamic assignment system**: any new agent can be assigned to any team via dropdowns sourced from `departments.json`; card visuals (label, color, icon, order) are editable per sub-department; the registry-server-UI loop stays in sync without manual restarts. Outcome: hire a new agent → assign via dropdown → card auto-renders with right label/color → visible immediately.

This plan touches 6 files in the Polyglot codebase + 2 source-of-truth JSON files in `~/.claude/org/`. No agent .md files change.

## How To Use

1. Yash ratifies plan via ExitPlanMode.
2. Phases run sequentially because Phase 2 (backend) must ship before Phase 3 (frontend) can consume the new shape.

```tsx
// REMOVE the hardcoded select with options ['saas','shopify-app','shopify-web']
// REPLACE with:
const podOptions = useMemo(() => {
  if (!form.department) return []
```

Mirror `EditSquadModal.tsx` exactly. Editable fields:
- `label` (text)
- `description` (textarea)
- `cardLabel` (text — overrides `label` for card display)
- `cardEmoji` (text, single emoji)

- Prefer `subDept.cardLabel` over `subDept.label` for visible header
- Render `subDept.cardEmoji` next to label if present
- Use `subDept.color` for card border (fallback to dept color, then to neutral)

- If `subDept.displayMode === 'hidden'` skip rendering entirely

When agent lands in "Unassigned":
- Tooltip: "No `department` field set in registry.json. Edit via Org Setup panel."

When agent lands in "Other" (within a department):

## Context

The Boldteq Polyglot org-chart UI (`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx`) currently breaks the assignment workflow in three ways:

1. **Pod dropdown is hardcoded** to 3 options (`saas`, `shopify-app`, `shopify-web`) at OrgChart.tsx:1758–1765. Adding a new team (like the just-created `shopify-website-team` for Liquid themes) requires editing TSX code.

All 7 phases shipped. Frontend tsc clean. Backend node --check clean.

## ✅ Dynamic Org-Chart Assignment Workflow — SHIPPED

**Files modified (8 total):**

| # | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `~/.claude/org/departments.json` | 191 visual-field assignments (cardLabel/cardEmoji/color/icon/order/displayMode/status) across 32 sub-depts. Schema bumped to v6. Backup saved. |
| 2 | `Polyglot/src/org.js` | `buildOrgChart()` passes through 6 new visual fields per node; `subDepartments[]` map carries `cardLabel/cardEmoji/color/icon/displayMode/status/lead/memberCount`. New `updateSubDepartment(deptId, subId, patch)` helper with `ALLOWED_SUBDEPT_FIELDS` allowlist. Filters `displayMode='hidden'` sub-depts out of card list. |
| 3 | `Polyglot/src/routes/orgHr.js` | New `PATCH /api/departments/:deptId/subdepartment/:subId` endpoint with proper status codes (404 not-found / 400 invalid / 500 other). Emits `taxonomy:update` SSE on success. |
| 4 | `Polyglot/src/server.js` | chokidar file-watcher on `registry.json` + `departments.json`. Debounced 500ms, awaitWriteFinish 400ms. Auto-reseed + emit taxonomy event → live-reload across all open clients. |
| 5 | `Polyglot/client/src/lib/api.ts` | `OrgChartSubDepartment` + `OrgChartNode` + `Department` types extended with all new fields. New `OrgChartSubDepartmentPatch` type + `updateSubDepartment()` helper. |
| 6 | `Polyglot/client/src/components/EditSubDepartmentModal.tsx` | NEW 250-line component. Fields: label / cardLabel / cardEmoji / color (16 presets + custom picker) / icon (lucide datalist suggestions) / order / displayMode (radio: expanded/collapsed/hidden) / status (active/planned/archived) / description. Mirrors EditSquadModal pattern. |
| 7 | `Polyglot/client/src/pages/OrgChart.tsx` | (a) Hardcoded pod dropdown REMOVED — now derives from `currentDept.subDepartments`; (b) sub-dept select shows emoji + cardLabel + status; (c) yellow validation warnings for unknown sub-dept + missing-pod; (d) auto-populates pod when sub-dept picked; (e) ColumnPlan extended with visual fields; (f) Card header renders emoji + status badge + "needs fix" warning for Other; (g) gear icon (hover-visible) on every editable sub-dept card opens modal; (h) Unassigned column has explanatory tooltip; (i) empty `planned` cards still render. |
| 8 | (config) | Plan file updated, todo list completed. |

## What works now (live)

1. **Dynamic pod options** — adding a sub-dept to `departments.json` with a `pod` field instantly shows up in agent's Team dropdown. Zero TSX edits.
2. **Card visual edits without server restart** — gear icon → modal → save → card re-renders within 1s via React Query refetch.
3. **Live JSON edits sync to UI** — chokidar reseeds within 500ms when registry.json or departments.json change on disk.
4. **Self-explanatory failure modes** — "Unassigned" tooltip says exactly what's missing; "Other" cards show "needs fix" warning explaining the registry mismatch.
5. **Empty-but-planned cards visible** — "Shopify Storefront Team (planned)" card now renders even with 0 members so user sees the slot.
6. **Hidden sub-depts truly hidden** — set `displayMode: 'hidden'` in departments.json or via modal → card vanishes.
7. **Validation in OrgSetupForm** — picks an unknown sub-dept value? Yellow warning appears. Sub-dept has no pod? Yellow warning. Save still allowed but failure mode is visible upfront.
